subject: Order Form — commitment tapering, invoice cadence & VAT evidence
messages:
From: Marta Silva <marta@acme.co>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoicing cadence, tapering of min-commit & VAT evidence

Hi Irene,

Thanks for getting the draft Order Form over to us. A couple of procurement items we need clarified before Legal/Finance will sign off: 

- We want the minimum commit to taper by quarter if usage drops below 40% of the forecasted baseline. Can Redwood reflect a quarterly taper mechanism rather than an all-or-nothing clawback?
- Invoice cadence: Acme prefers quarterly invoices in arrears, but your order form currently lists monthly invoicing. Can we reconcile to quarterly (with one invoice per quarter) and include a line-item schedule for anticipated invoice dates?
- VAT / tax evidence: our Finance team requires a VAT registration doc for Redwood in the EU or a statement that Redwood will remit VAT. Can you provide the certificate or guidance on whether Acme should self-assess VAT?

Attached: ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf (we annotated a couple of pricing rows).

We'd like to close the commercials this week if possible — any chance you can confirm an approach and loop in legal?

Best,
Marta
Marta Silva
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Silva <marta@acme.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence, tapering of min-commit & VAT evidence

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated PDF. Quick answers and proposed next steps below. I’ll keep this high level and let Markus call the legal language.

1) Minimum-commit tapering: we can accept a quarterly taper based on realized usage, with a floor (no taper below 25% of baseline). Proposal: if average utilization across the quarter < 40% of baseline, the min-commit reduces by 20% the following quarter, subject to a one-time contract amendment per 12-month period. That gives Acme predictability and prevents repeated erosion.

2) Invoice cadence: we’re generally set up for monthly invoices but can support quarterly invoicing in arrears. Operationally, we’d split charges by month internally and aggregate into a single quarterly invoice; that will be reflected in the Order Form's "Invoicing Schedule" appendix. Please confirm the preferred quarter end dates (we assumed Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec).

3) VAT evidence: we need to confirm with Finance whether Redwood will issue VAT-inclusive invoices or provide a VAT registration certificate. Kimberly — can you attach the EU VAT cert we already have on file for EU entities? If we cannot produce a local registration certificate, we will include a statement in the order form that Acme is responsible for applicable VAT self-assessment.

Markus — from Legal: are you comfortable with the "one-time amendment per 12-months" operationally, or do you prefer a fixed clawback formula? Also see Marta's annotation on pricing row 2 — we may need a small redline.

If everyone is aligned I can produce a narrow redline (OrderForm_v3 -> v4) and send to Acme for signature.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Silva <marta@acme.co>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 14:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence, tapering of min-commit & VAT evidence

Irene / team — thanks. Quick legal read and suggested contract language (high level). I attached a tracked-comments doc (redline_orderform_remarks.docx).

- Tapering mechanism: Acceptable in principle. Recommended language: "If the Customer's trailing three-month average usage falls below forty percent (40%) of the agreed baseline, the Parties shall agree to a one-time reduction of up to twenty percent (20%) of the Minimum Commitment for the next consecutive quarter, provided such reduction may occur no more than once in any rolling twelve (12) month period." Keeps it limited and enforceable.
- Invoice cadence: Approve quarterly invoicing in arrears. Add: "Invoices will be issued on the business day following quarter end; payment terms remain net 30 unless otherwise agreed in writing." Note: finance prefers not to change Net-30 in the Order Form without CFO approval.
- VAT / tax evidence: We do not currently have a universal EU VAT registration to issue across all regions. Kimberly — please attach the VAT registration for our Luxembourg entity (if available). Otherwise, propose clause: "Customer shall be responsible for any VAT or other similar taxes due in Customer's jurisdiction, unless Redwood issues a VAT-inclusive invoice where applicable."

Operational caveats: we should avoid a clause that creates an open-ended right to reduce the commitment multiple times. The one-time-per-12-month limit above addresses that. Also suggest a Schedule that enumerates "Invoice Dates" so accounting has a clear timeline.

Irene — I can produce a short Order Form redline (v4) reflecting these three bullets; I will include bracketed MSA references for the clawback/adjustment interaction (see MSA §4.2 and §7.1).

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_orderform_remarks.docx (comment highlights), [stub] VAT_Registration_Acme.pdf (quoted by Acme)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Silva <marta@acme.co>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence, tapering of min-commit & VAT evidence

Hi Marta — following up after Markus's comments. Short operational plan: 

- We'll publish Order Form v4 with the tapered-commit language Markus included and an "Invoice Schedule" appendix listing quarter end invoice dates (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec).
- We will keep Net-30 as standard. If Acme needs Net-45/Net-60 we can escalate to Finance, but please flag now so we can parallel the sign-off path.
- VAT: Kimberly please attach Redwood's Luxembourg VAT cert if available. If not, we will add the clause that makes Acme responsible for VAT self-assessment. Acme — if you prefer Redwood to handle VAT, expect a short conversation with Finance about local registration and potential administrative lead time.

Next step: Irene will send v4 (narrow redline) by Monday morning with the three changes. Marta — if you and your Legal want to propose alternate wording for the tapering % or the once-per-12-month limit, happy to review quickly; we'll aim to keep this limited and get signatures this week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
